Anything the owner must do before a number can exist is left blank on purpose.

facts.fact: Break-even win probability at -110 on both sides
facts.note: Computed as 110/210 from the price; the academic sample cited here independently states a 52.38% break-even threshold for the same price structure, which is the arithmetic agreement this site checks its own formulas against.

facts.fact: Overround of a -110 / -110 two-way market and the balanced theoretical hold
facts.note: 2 x 1/1.9091 = 1.0476. If the book is balanced it keeps about 2.4% of handle; a one-sided book keeps the full 4.76%. Any strategy whose claimed edge is under ~2.5% is inside the cost band on this price.

facts.fact: Home teams beating the spread, 2002-2011 (2,560 games, regular season and postseason)
facts.note: Reported in the paper's abstract; it is a decade-old sample and is quoted as context for how small apparent biases are, not as an actionable number for 2026.

facts.fact: Cumulative hit rate of a 2002-2011 home-underdog strategy reported by the same paper
facts.note: Against a 52.38% break-even. Note what this means: a well-known 'system' with a published edge of about one point over break-even - and the sample ends in 2011. It is an illustration of how thin these things are, not an invitation.

facts.fact: League tracking data (Next Gen Stats) availability
facts.note: Official league documentation also states box score and play-by-play update live during the game, and that preseason film and data are not available in the NFL Pro product. Any pre-kickoff snap projection therefore has no official same-day source.

facts.fact: Documented NFL feed coverage: moneyline, spreads, totals, quarter/half, player props (US and AU books), historical from mid-2020 for the featured markets
facts.value: Confirmed by the vendor's own documentation
facts.note: Availability of a field is not quality, depth or licence permission. Prop history depth is the specific thing to test in a trial, because prop strategies are the least supportable without it (Q-01).

facts.fact: League roster rules governing unavailability: IR has no list limit but eight return designations per club, a four-game minimum, two designations per player; PUP/NFI activation after four games; 16-man practice squads; three elevations per player per season
facts.note: The official article is written around the 2022 offseason; the 2026 wording must be re-confirmed (Q-09, IR-029). These rules are what turn an injury into a dated absence window.

facts.fact: Injury report vocabulary: Did Not Participate / Limited (under 100% of normal reps) / Full (100%); game status Out / Doubtful / Questionable; 'Probable' abolished because about 95% of Probable players played; a certain-to-play player is not listed at all, and deactivating him then requires an explanation to the league
facts.note: This is the reason a blank game status must be stored as a coded state ('no designation') and never read as 'unavailable' or as 'missing'.

facts.fact: Correlated multi-leg tickets: outside a Same Game or Progressive Parlay, a parlay with two or more correlated selections may be void; a non-SGP parlay 'shall never include two or more offers where the outcomes of which might turn out to be related'; a void or push leg reprices a pre-live SGP and an all-void/push ticket is void
facts.note: Read from the search rendering of a licensed casino's published copy of the operator's rules (v15), not from a document retrieved by this session. Rules vary by operator and state; gate G-12 requires reading the operator that will actually settle the bet (Q-07).

facts.fact: A state rule requires that an operator accept a wager only where the outcome can be verified, can be generated by a reliable and independent process, is not affected by any wager placed, and the event complies with applicable law; the commission may disapprove a data source
facts.note: The retrieved text is the 2020 emergency rule; the codified current version should be read from the commission's own register (Q-12, Q-13). Quoted to show that settlement and data provenance are regulated subjects, which limits any 'we settle it ourselves' plan.

facts.fact: The regulator that publishes the Colorado data cited above publishes the help instruction on the same page: problem-gambling resources at BetSmart.Colorado.gov and 'call or text 1-800-GAMBLER'
facts.note: Carried in the footer of every page in this section because the same regulator frames its own market data that way.
